gaps.sentence: I must ___ my homework before I can go out.
gaps.explanation: do homework is the fixed collocation; 'make homework' is a common learner error.

gaps.sentence: She ___ no difficulty finding the address.
gaps.hint: fixed pattern: ___ no difficulty doing something
gaps.explanation: have no difficulty (in) doing something is the fixed pattern; 'made no difficulty' is wrong.

gaps.sentence: They ___ a lot of business with companies in Asia.
gaps.explanation: do business with somebody is the fixed expression for commercial activity.

gaps.sentence: Most children learn to ___ the time before they start school.
gaps.hint: fixed phrase: ___ the time (read a clock)
gaps.explanation: tell the time means to be able to read a clock; it is a fixed expression.

gaps.sentence: Over five hundred athletes will ___ part in the games.
gaps.explanation: take part in something means to participate in it.

gaps.sentence: We ___ to the conclusion that the project was not viable.
gaps.explanation: come to the conclusion that ... is the fixed phrase; 'reach' and 'arrive' do not take 'to'.

gaps.sentence: We were asked to ___ an experiment in the laboratory.
gaps.explanation: do an experiment is the standard collocation in scientific contexts.

gaps.sentence: The boy knew it was wrong to ___ lies.
gaps.explanation: tell a lie / tell lies is the fixed collocation; a base verb is needed after 'to'.
